definitions.explanation: Not of the highest quality or rank. Used to describe people, things, or organizations that fall short of top-tier standards.

examples.japanese: {二流|にりゅう}の{選手|せんしゅ}では{勝|か}てない。
あの{会社|かいしゃ}は{二流|にりゅう}だと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: That company is said to be second-rate.

examples.japanese: {一流|いちりゅう}の{技術|ぎじゅつ}がなくても、{二流|にりゅう}で{終|お}わりたくないという{気持|きも}ちが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: Even without top-tier skills, the desire not to end up second-rate is what matters.

notes:
USAGE:
{二流|にりゅう} is generally negative, implying that something or someone does not meet the highest standard. It is used with の to modify nouns.
While {二流|にりゅう} literally means "second tier," it carries a negative connotation of being mediocre or not good enough. It is more blunt than {平凡|へいぼん} (ordinary) and less harsh than {三流|さんりゅう}.

RELATED WORDS:
- {一流|いちりゅう} (first-rate, top-class)
- {三流|さんりゅう} (third-rate, low-quality — more strongly negative)
- {超一流|ちょういちりゅう} (world-class, top-tier)
